text:
elaine: Heads-up — after today's coral-v2 onboarding we see a p99 spike on the short-sequence perf suite for staging. Rolling back the model clears it. Opening a thread to bisect.

mike: Seen it. p50 fine, p99 ~2.4x on 1–16 token buckets. CI perf job failed for the staging bump too. Attaching quick perf summary I pulled from the run.

sasha: Logs look like a ton of KV cache evictions on the hot path. I think batching heuristics are producing more small bursts which thrash the cache and trigger a switch to the long-seq kernel.

elaine: here's the profiling snippet that highlights kernel selection toggles (from the failing staging run):
```
[profiling] request_id=0x7f8a kernel=short_seq selected_count=120
[profiling] request_id=0x7f8b kernel=long_seq selected_count=98
[kv] cache_hits=1200 cache_misses=980 evictions=432
```

ivy: interesting — the tokenizer change in coral-v2 adds an extra <sep> token in many prompts, which can bump effective sequence length for short prompts. Could be a config drift: tokenizer.max_context or eos handling.

mike: good call. I diffed the tokenizer config between coral-v1 and coral-v2:
```
- truncate_mode: tail
- eos_token: "<|endoftext|>"
+ truncate_mode: head
+ eos_token: "<sep>"
```
That head-truncation plus extra <sep> moves padding earlier and increases prefix diversity -> worse cache reuse.

sasha: Also noticed batching heuristic change in last runtime PR: it now groups by arrival window with a 3ms min-batch delay when throughput low. With coral-v2 we'll see more variable token lengths so the heuristic is choosing to flush earlier. That reduces kernel amortization.

elaine: action items: 1) bisect runtime PRs around batching heuristics, 2) try a staging rollout pinning coral-v2 tokenizer to coral-v1 config (quick test), 3) add KV eviction counters to the per-route console.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: staging/coral-v2 deployed by ci-bot@deploys at 1948123420

mike: quick repro command for local perf suite (comes from the job):
```
./run_perf --model coral-v2 --sequence_lengths 1,4,8,16 --concurrency 32 --trace kernel
```

ivy: I can run that with coral-v1 tokenizer overlay and post numbers. If we see p99 go down that points at tokenizer drift.

sasha: I'll start the bisect for runtime PRs 5123..5178 focusing on batching heuristics and kernel routing changes. ETA ~45m for first pass.

elaine: thanks — if bisect points to runtime, we should hotfix the batching window revert and then re-onboard coral-v2 after adjusting tokenizer config.

mike: also adding a guard in rollout: if p99 increases >30% in 30m, auto-revert. We didn't have that gated for this bump — adding the monitor now.

ivy: initial quick test: coral-v1 tokenizer overlay dropped staging p99 by ~28% on short-seq. I pushed the numbers to the perf dashboard.

elaine: nice! sounds like tokenizer/eos config is the main suspect. sasha, keep us posted on the bisect. If runtime is also contributing we may need a two-pronged fix (heuristic tweak + tokenizer fix).

sasha: bisect shows the heuristic tweak PR 5149 changes batch flush timing and correlates with p99 spikes when arrival variance high. Reverting 5149 locally restores expected p99.

elaine: decision: revert 5149 from runtime for now, pin tokenizer eos to coral-v1 behavior in staging, and re-evaluate with a controlled rollout for coral-v2. I'll open the revert PR and the rollout plan.

mike: I'll open the monitor/alert and add the KV eviction graph to the route dashboard. Also adding a small e2e that runs the short-seq perf smoke on every model onboard CI job.

elaine: thanks team. Follow-ups: PRs for revert + tokenizer pin, perf smoke in onboard CI, KV eviction dashboard. Marking this thread as the blocker for coral-v2 rollout. :thumbsup:
